light: harsh cold light from high windows on the left, deep shadows, a red-tinted dramatic mood
bg: Interior of the meeting hall in the Theatre of Pompey in Rome, 44 BC: tall marble columns, a raised marble statue of Pompey the Great in a toga standing on a pedestal at the right, stone benches, shafts of light from high windows, dust in the air.
mid: In the centre of the frame, medium size: Julius Caesar, balding older Roman in a white toga with a purple border and a gold laurel wreath, recoiling backward with one arm raised to shield himself, a shocked betrayed expression. Around him in a tight ring, six Roman senators in white togas, their faces hard, each with a short dagger raised high above their heads. No blood, no wounds.
fg: Very close to the viewer at the left and right edges of the frame, cut off by the frame: the dark backs, shoulders and heads of two senators in togas seen from behind, each raising a dagger, almost silhouettes. The whole middle of the frame stays empty.
